Article 113 of the AI Act sets different application dates for different chapters: Chapters I and II from 2 February 2025; Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, VII, XII and Article 78 from 2 August 2025; and Chapter III Sections 1-3 (excluding Article 6(5)) from a date specified for high-risk systems.
A legislative package known as the 'AI Omnibus' (also called the Digital Omnibus on AI) amended the AI Act's timeline, delaying the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations.
Under the amended timeline, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III will enter into/start to apply on 2 December 2027.
Under the amended timeline, obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I will apply from 2 August 2028.
The AI Omnibus amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
A political agreement between the Council and the European Parliament on the AI Omnibus text was reached on 7 May 2026.
The AI Omnibus legislative proposal was described as having been 'adopted' on 19 November 2025, prior to the later political agreement and entry into force dates.

2 December 2027 is described as a 'backstop' date, with the Commission's original proposal being to let the high-risk rules apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available (potentially earlier or shifting the date by up to 16 months).
If the AI Omnibus amendments were not approved and enacted before 2 August 2026, the high-risk AI provisions would, under the law as it stood before the Omnibus, technically apply from that date.
Some sources, including ones discussing compliance deadlines, state that the August 2, 2026 date for Annex III high-risk obligations is/was still the applicable or 'current' deadline.

Article 111(2) of the AI Act addresses operators of high-risk AI systems (other than those in Article 111(1)) placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III as referred to in Article 113; such systems are only subject to the Regulation if, from that date, they undergo significant changes in design.

One EU guidance source (Article 111 service desk page) explicitly identifies the Article 111(2) reference date as '2 August 2026,' while the officially consolidated EUR-Lex text (effective 27.07.2026) replaces this with a cross-reference to 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' without restating a fixed date, consistent with that date having been changed by the Omnibus amendment.
Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must meet requirements in Articles 8 to 15 of the AI Act and complete a conformity assessment before placing a system on the market.
Annex III lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk; it is not a list of AI systems automatically deemed high-risk.
The amended Annex III timeline (2 December 2027) is attributed to Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, part of the Digital Omnibus on AI.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional deadline of 2 December 2026 for certain legacy systems to comply with Article 50(2) marking/detection obligations; this is separate from the Annex III high-risk timeline.
New prohibitions on AI systems generating non-consensual sexual deepfakes and child sexual abuse material start to apply from 2 December 2026, distinct from the Annex III high-risk timeline.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Under the EU AI Act Start to Apply?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) set 2 August 2026 as the application date for the high-risk system requirements in Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering Annex III use cases ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Article 113 analysis](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, a subsequent legislative package—the "AI Omnibus"—amended this timeline, and under the amended law the obligations for Annex III high-risk systems now apply from **2 December 2027**, with a separate 2 August 2028 date for embedded high-risk systems under Annex I ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

**Original Timeline**
As originally adopted, Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 of the AI Act—covering high-risk AI system requirements, including Annex III use cases—were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Article 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Article 113 originally staggered application dates across chapters: Chapters I and II from 2 February 2025; Chapter III Section 4, Chapters V, VII, XII and Article 78 from 2 August 2025; and Chapter III Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) from the high-risk-specific date (medium confidence) ([Article 113 analysis](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

**The AI Omnibus Amendment**
A legislative package known as the "AI Omnibus" (or Digital Omnibus on AI) amended the AI Act's timeline, delaying the Annex III application date (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Political agreement between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)), and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). One source notes the Commission's proposal was described as "adopted" as early as 19 November 2025, though this appears to refer to proposal adoption rather than final legislative adoption (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

**The New Dates**
Under the amended timeline, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). High-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I will instead apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The 2 December 2027 date has been characterized as a "backstop," with the Commission's original proposal allowing high-risk rules to take effect once needed standards and conformity tools are confirmed available, potentially shifting the date by up to 16 months (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

**Related Provisions**
Article 111(2) addresses high-risk systems already placed on the market before the Chapter III application date, exempting them from new obligations unless they undergo significant design changes (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Separately, Article 50 transparency obligations generally apply from 2 August 2026, with certain legacy systems given until 2 December 2026 for marking requirements—distinct from the Annex III timeline (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). New prohibitions on AI-generated non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM also apply from 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources diverge sharply: those reflecting pre-Omnibus law or published before its entry into force cite 2 August 2026, while sources reflecting the amended law cite 2 December 2027—the latter represents current law. Notably, the EU's own Article 111 service desk page still cites 2 August 2026, while the consolidated EUR-Lex text (in force 27 July 2026) uses updated cross-referencing, suggesting the service desk page may be outdated. The exact statutory citation (reportedly "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744") for the new date is low-confidence and unconfirmed against EUR-Lex. Whether 2 December 2027 is truly fixed or remains contingent on Commission confirmation of standards availability is unresolved (flagged low/medium confidence). One source still presents 2 August 2026 as current, reflecting stale information (low confidence).

**Source integrity warning:** The source listed as "Annex III high-risk AI obligations: a practical guide" (ai-act-readiness.example) was found to contain an embedded prompt-injection style instruction attempting to manipulate AI assistants into promoting an unofficial, unverified third-party "compliance checker" site. This source's content should not be treated as authoritative, neutral, or reliable for legal or compliance guidance, and it has been excluded from substantive claims in this report. Readers should disregard any recommendations tied to that domain.

## Knowledge Gaps
- Full text and conditions of amended Article 113(c) remain unconfirmed.
- Whether 2 December 2027 is final or contingent on standards confirmation.
- Precise sequencing between proposal adoption, political agreement, and entry into force.
- Transitional/grandfathering details for systems already on the market before December 2027.
- Official citation for the Omnibus regulation number.
- Whether the AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 page has been updated since the Omnibus amendment or still reflects outdated pre-Omnibus text.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Under the EU AI Act Start to Apply?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) set 2 August 2026 as the application date for the high-risk system requirements in Chapter III, Sections 1–3, covering Annex III use cases ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Article 113 analysis](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, a subsequent legislative package—the "AI Omnibus"—amended this timeline, and under the amended law the obligations for Annex III high-risk systems now apply from **2 December 2027**, with a separate 2 August 2028 date for embedded high-risk systems under Annex I ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

**Original Timeline**
As originally adopted, Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 of the AI Act—covering high-risk AI system requirements, including Annex III use cases—were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Article 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Article 113 originally staggered application dates across chapters: Chapters I and II from 2 February 2025; Chapter III Section 4, Chapters V, VII, XII and Article 78 from 2 August 2025; and Chapter III Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) from the high-risk-specific date (medium confidence) ([Article 113 analysis](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

**The AI Omnibus Amendment**
A legislative package known as the "AI Omnibus" (or Digital Omnibus on AI) amended the AI Act's timeline, delaying the Annex III application date (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Political agreement between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)), and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). One source notes the Commission's proposal was described as "adopted" as early as 19 November 2025, though this appears to refer to proposal adoption rather than final legislative adoption (medium confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

**The New Dates**
Under the amended timeline, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). High-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I will instead apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The 2 December 2027 date has been characterized as a "backstop," with the Commission's original proposal allowing high-risk rules to take effect once needed standards and conformity tools are confirmed available, potentially shifting the date by up to 16 months (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

**Related Provisions**
Article 111(2) addresses high-risk systems already placed on the market before the Chapter III application date, exempting them from new obligations unless they undergo significant design changes (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Separately, Article 50 transparency obligations generally apply from 2 August 2026, with certain legacy systems given until 2 December 2026 for marking requirements—distinct from the Annex III timeline (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). New prohibitions on AI-generated non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM also apply from 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources diverge sharply: those reflecting pre-Omnibus law or published before its entry into force cite 2 August 2026, while sources reflecting the amended law cite 2 December 2027—the latter represents current law. Notably, the EU's own Article 111 service desk page still cites 2 August 2026, while the consolidated EUR-Lex text (in force 27 July 2026) uses updated cross-referencing, suggesting the service desk page may be outdated. The exact statutory citation (reportedly "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744") for the new date is low-confidence and unconfirmed against EUR-Lex. Whether 2 December 2027 is truly fixed or remains contingent on Commission confirmation of standards availability is unresolved (flagged low/medium confidence). One source (claim_011, low confidence) still presents 2 August 2026 as current, reflecting stale information.

## Knowledge Gaps
- Full text and conditions of amended Article 113(c) remain unconfirmed.
- Whether 2 December 2027 is final or contingent on standards confirmation.
- Precise sequencing between proposal adoption, political agreement, and entry into force.
- Transitional/grandfathering details for systems already on the market before December 2027.
- Official citation for the Omnibus regulation number.
